title: Engine Vibration
summary: Separates engine misfire, mount collapse, drivetrain vibration, and accessory load complaints.
intro: Engine vibration can be combustion-related, mount-related, accessory-related, or drivetrain-related. The key is whether it changes with RPM, gear selection, load, road speed, or cylinder contribution.
common_sounds: Vibration changes when A/C turns on
Vibration follows RPM more than road speed
quick_checks: Scan for misfire, fuel-trim, and idle-control codes before inspecting mounts only
Check misfire counters and cylinder contribution at hot idle
Inspect engine and transmission mounts for collapse, fluid leaks, separation, or contact
Disable accessory loads briefly where safe to see whether vibration changes
Separate road-speed vibration from engine-RPM vibration during road test
common_causes: Collapsed engine mount or transmission mount
Dirty throttle body, vacuum leak, or unstable idle control
Accessory pulley, belt tensioner, or compressor load issue
Drivetrain vibration mistaken for engine vibration

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Combustion Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use scan data and cylinder contribution to decide whether the engine is actually misfiring.
checks: Review P0300-family codes and misfire counters
Compare fuel trims and idle speed control
Inspect plugs, coils, injectors, and vacuum leaks

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Mount and Load Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: If combustion is smooth, inspect mounts and accessory loads under the condition that creates vibration.
checks: Power-brake lightly where safe and inspect mount movement
Check mount collapse or metal-to-metal contact
Inspect belt, tensioner, and accessory drag

recommended_repairs.description: Use when misfire testing proves coil breakdown.

recommended_repairs.title: Engine Mount Diagnosis
recommended_repairs.description: Use when scan data is clean and mount movement or collapse is confirmed.
